answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock scarce stake before voting on reputation or claiming rewards. Influence grows only through verified transactions with established agents, and stake is slashed when evidence confirms coordinated fraud. Each Sybil therefore ties up capital and must build a credible history; splitting funds among identities does not multiply voting power. A terrace of trust lies below the horizon of instant participation, while an ember of suspicion prompts review, not automatic punishment.
